name: West Virginia
nameStory: West Virginia is the state that seceded from a secession. When Virginia left the Union in 1861, the mountain counties in the west - too steep for plantations, with few enslaved people and long-standing resentment of the coastal planters who ran the state - refused to go along and broke away to form their own state.
capitalStory: Charleston sits where the Elk River meets the Kanawha, named for an early settler's father. The capital bounced back and forth between Wheeling and Charleston twice before the argument was finally settled by popular vote in 1877.

majorFeatures.name: Appalachian Mountains
majorFeatures.note: The entire state sits inside them

majorFeatures.name: New River Gorge
majorFeatures.note: One of the oldest rivers on the continent

funFacts: West Virginia is the only state entirely within the Appalachian mountains.
It has the highest average elevation of any state east of the Mississippi.
The New River is misnamed - it is one of the oldest rivers in the world, older than the mountains it cuts through, and it flows north.
The state has two panhandles, and almost none of its border is a straight line; it follows rivers and ridges the whole way around.
whyItMatters: In 1921 roughly 10,000 coal miners fought company forces and federal troops at Blair Mountain in the largest armed labor uprising in US history. Coal shaped the state's politics, its economy, and now its hardest question: what a place does when the one industry it was built on winds down.
